The sim-to-real gap introduces uncertainty: collision detection precision and contact dynamics differ on physical hardware, and action-collapse severity may vary with real-world noise and latency. However, the core diagnostic insight---that near-zero motor output inflates CAR---is kinematic and does not depend on sim-to-real transfer; dfCAR remains applicable on physical platforms given EE position logging.

Statistical power is limited by $n{=}3$ seeds per condition (MDE ${\approx}$ 5.6\,pp at 80\% power). Oracle experiments used largely action-collapsed baselines; the EE-only refinement failure may interact differently with actively moving policies where joint-space coupling produces larger displacements. Validation on non-collapsed policies and full-body SDF supervision remain necessary before generalizing the counterproductive finding. Tasks involving multi-arm coordination or cluttered environments may exhibit different collision patterns; our structural argument should strengthen in such settings, but empirical confirmation is needed.
